summary: Provider trust maps can be assembled from vendor assurance data, continuous third-party risk records and policy-as-code enforcement. These tools cover provider evidence and runtime decisions; the organization must still define its own data classes, tasks and acceptable residual risk.

items.text: Cloud Security Alliance STAR is a public registry of cloud-provider security and privacy assurance, including self-assessments, third-party certifications and continuous assurance levels. Its control evidence can populate the provider side of a trust map instead of relying on model-brand reputation.

OneTrust Third-Party Risk Management maintains a vendor inventory, assigns risk tiers, runs assessments and monitors changes and issues. Those capabilities support per-provider evidence, review dates and escalation triggers rather than a one-time allowlist.

Open Policy Agent evaluates declarative Rego policies over structured JSON input and returns machine-readable decisions. A gateway can use it to enforce that task fit, model trust, provider trust, data class and requested capability all satisfy the map before dispatch.
